steps.subject: [Offload] Fix pessimistic max block count sizing on AMDGPU (#204242)

model_frontier_decision.reason: semantic leader confidence meets threshold; use semantic top-k

evidence: AMDGPU offload runtime launch sizing does not match a MemorySSA verification crash
Changes plugin interface and block-count policy, far from LLVM optimizer memory dependence analysis
features: offload runtime, AMDGPU launch configuration, block limit sizing
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Refactors offload runtime block-count sizing so the device launch limit depends on the requested thread count instead of using a fixed maximum-teams cap. The generic device interface now exposes a virtual getBlockLimit(NumThreads) hook, and the AMDGPU implementation computes a grid-size-based block limit from maximum teams multiplied by thread limit, clamped to 32 bits. Kernel launch sizing paths are updated to pass EffectiveNumThreads when clamping explicit or preferred block counts, reducing overly pessimistic block truncation on AMDGPU.
Mechanisms: device launch configuration sizing; virtual interface expansion; AMDGPU-specific occupancy/grid limit calculation; kernel block-count clamping policy
Touched symbols: GenericDeviceTy::getBlockLimit; AMDGPUDeviceTy::getBlockLimit; GenericKernelTy::getEffectiveNumBlocks; GridValues.GV_Max_Teams; getThreadLimit
Risk relevance: Changes runtime policy for kernel launch dimensions and block limits; Affects code paths that compute effective execution configuration from user input and device caps; Incorrect sizing here can alter kernel behavior or expose latent launch/configuration bugs
Build risk: Interface change requires recompilation across offload plugin code; Adds a virtual override and new call sites with thread-count plumbing; AMDGPU-specific runtime logic may be sensitive to platform assumptions and integer-width limits

top_candidates.subject: [MLIR][XeGPU] Fix load_matrix lowering for non-LLVM element types (#203629)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Updates XeGPU-to-XeVM lowering for matrix load/store so the emitted LLVM load type comes from the type converter rather than from the source result element type. This changes lowering of non-LLVM-representable element types by mapping them to storage integers of the same bit width, and preserves the special-case collapse of size-1 vectors to scalars via the converter. The accompanying test adds scalar and vector load cases for f8E8M0FNU to verify the legal LLVM IR shape and the post-load bitcast/vector-broadcast reconstruction.
Mechanisms: MLIR conversion legality/type materialization; type conversion for unsupported element types; scalar vs vector load lowering; bitcast/broadcast reconstruction after integer storage load
Touched symbols: LoadStoreMatrixToXeVMPattern; LLVM::LoadOp::create; getTypeConverter()->convertType; xegpu.load_matrix
Risk relevance: Touches lowering logic for load/store formation and type legality; Changes how vector<1x...> and exotic element types are represented in generated IR; Could affect downstream canonicalization or verifier behavior for memory operations in conversion pipelines
Build risk: Adds new conversion/test coverage for f8E8M0FNU storage mapping; Exercises target-specific lowering paths and LLVM dialect type conversion; Potentially sensitive to type-converter assumptions across backends

[SimpleLoopUnswitch] Generalize the notion of trivial unswitching (#193989)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Extends SimpleLoopUnswitch’s notion of trivial unswitching to handle invariant branches that target a loop latch, not just loop exits, by rewiring a latch edge to the unique loop exit when the latch is side-effect free and the loop is proven finite. The new path updates CFG edges, phi incoming values, DominatorTree, and optionally MemorySSA via applyUpdates before allowing the normal trivial-unswitch logic to proceed. The patch also tightens bookkeeping with a ModifiedBranch flag and asserts to catch cases where the branch CFG is rewritten without actually completing an unswitch.
Mechanisms: loop unswitching CFG rewrite; latch-to-exit edge redirection; dominance tree update; MemorySSA update application; finite-loop guard via ScalarEvolution backedge count
Touched symbols: unswitchTrivialBranch; areLoopExitPHIsLoopInvariant; L.getLoopLatch; L.getUniqueLatchExitBlock; SCEV; MSSAU->applyUpdates; DominatorTree::applyUpdates
Risk relevance: Directly mutates loop CFG and MemorySSA-relevant edges, matching crash-prone optimizer infrastructure; Introduces new control-flow rewrites in the same area as invariant-branch handling and dominance verification; Adds assertions around partial CFG mutation, which can surface latent verification failures if updates are inconsistent
Build risk: Touches core scalar transform code and many phase-ordering tests; Adds a new dedicated regression test with numerous CFG shapes and update-sensitive cases; MemorySSA/DominatorTree update paths are high-risk for verifier or analysis consistency regressions
